{"questions": [
{
"id": "p1",
"topic": "lattice points on a circle (sums of two squares)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Consider the lattice points (x, y) with x > 0 and y > 0 that lie on the circle x² + y² = 1105. Find the sum of the x-coordinates of these points.",
"answer": 168,
"target_wrong": 121,
"error_description": "The representation 1105 = 23² + 24² is left out (the search 1105 − k² is stopped before k = 23), so the points (23, 24) and (24, 23) are missing and the sum is 4+33+9+32+12+31 = 121 instead of 168.",
"cases": ["(4,33)", "(33,4)", "(9,32)", "(32,9)", "(12,31)", "(31,12)", "(23,24)", "(24,23)"],
"solution": "We need positive integers x, y with x² + y² = 1105 = 5·13·17. Since 1105 has three distinct prime factors all ≡ 1 (mod 4), it has 4·8 = 32 lattice points on the circle, none on the axes, hence 8 in the open first quadrant. Checking 1105 − k² for k = 1, 2, …, 23 (we only need k ≤ 23 since 2·23² < 1105 < 2·24²): 1105 − 16 = 1089 = 33², 1105 − 81 = 1024 = 32², 1105 − 144 = 961 = 31², 1105 − 529 = 576 = 24², and no other k works. So the representations are 4² + 33², 9² + 32², 12² + 31², 23² + 24², giving the eight points (4,33), (33,4), (9,32), (32,9), (12,31), (31,12), (23,24), (24,23). The sum of the x-coordinates is 4+33+9+32+12+31+23+24 = 168.",
"check_code": "import math\nn=1105\ns=0\nfor x in range(1,n):\n    y2=n-x*x\n    if y2<=0: continue\n    y=math.isqrt(y2)\n    if y*y==y2: s+=x\nprint(s)"

{
"id": "p2",
"topic": "integer distances from the origin to lattice points on a vertical line",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Find the sum of the distinct positive integers that occur as the distance from the origin to a lattice point on the line x = 36.",
"answer": 865,
"target_wrong": 829,
"error_description": "The boundary case y = 0 (the point (36, 0) itself, distance 36, coming from the square factor pair 18·18 of 324) is omitted; only the seven pairs with s < t are listed, giving 829 instead of 865.",
"cases": ["1·324 → d = 325", "2·162 → d = 164", "3·108 → d = 111", "4·81 → d = 85", "6·54 → d = 60", "9·36 → d = 45", "12·27 → d = 39", "18·18 → d = 36 (y = 0)"],
"solution": "A lattice point on x = 36 is (36, y) and its distance to the origin is d = √(1296 + y²). We need d² − y² = 1296, i.e. (d − y)(d + y) = 1296 with d ≥ |y| ≥ 0. Since 1296 is even and d − y, d + y have the same parity, both are even: write d − y = 2s, d + y = 2t with st = 324, s ≤ t. The factor pairs of 324 = 2²·3⁴ with s ≤ t are (1,324), (2,162), (3,108), (4,81), (6,54), (9,36), (12,27), (18,18), and d = s + t gives 325, 164, 111, 85, 60, 45, 39, 36 respectively (the last is the point (36, 0)). All eight distances are distinct, and their sum is 325+164+111+85+60+45+39+36 = 865.",
"check_code": "import math\ns=set()\nfor y in range(0,1300):\n    d2=36*36+y*y\n    d=math.isqrt(d2)\n    if d*d==d2: s.add(d)\nprint(sum(s))"

"topic": "lattice points in a disk with half-integer center",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "How many lattice points lie inside or on the circle with center (1/2, 1/2) and radius 5/√2?",

Put u = 2x − 1, v = 2y − 1; these are odd integers and (x, y) ↔ (u, v) is a bijection between lattice points and pairs of odd integers. The odd squares at most 50 are 1, 9, 25, 49. The ordered pairs (u², v²) with sum ≤ 50 are (1,1), (1,9), (9,1), (1,25), (25,1), (1,49), (49,1), (9,9), (9,25), (25,9), (25,25) — eleven pairs, where (1,49) and (25,25) give equality (points on the circle). "question": "Let S be the set of positive integers c for which there exists a right triangle whose two legs lie along the coordinate axes, whose three vertices are lattice points, whose inscribed circle has radius 6, and whose hypotenuse has length c. Find the sum of the elements of S.",

"target_wrong": 238,
"error_description": "The factor pair 8·9 of 72 (giving legs 20, 21 and hypotenuse 29) is left out of the list (1,72), (2,36), (3,24), (4,18), (6,12), so the sum is 85+50+39+34+30 = 238 instead of 267.",

From a² + b² = (a + b − 12)² we get 0 = −24a − 24b + 144 + 2ab, i.e. ab − 12a − 12b + 72 = 0, so (a − 12)(b − 12) = 72. Both factors must be positive (if both were negative, a, b < 12 would give a + b < c + 12 contradiction with c > 0 and the triangle inequality forces a + b > c, so a + b − 12 = c < a + b; in fact a − 12 < 0 would force b − 12 < 0 and then a, b < 12, c = a + b − 12 < a, impossible). With a ≤ b the factor pairs of 72 are (1,72), (2,36), (3,24), (4,18), (6,12), (8,9), giving (a, b, c) = (13,84,85), (14,48,50), (15,36,39), (16,30,34), (18,24,30), (20,21,29). "question": "How many squares have all four vertices in the set of lattice points {(x, y) : 0 ≤ x ≤ 4, 0 ≤ y ≤ 4}?",

Its axis-parallel bounding box is a (p+q)×(p+q) square, and the square fits in the 5×5 point grid in exactly (5 − (p+q))² positions when p + q ≤ 4. Summing over side vectors: p+q = 1: (1,0) → 16; p+q = 2: (2,0), (1,1) → 9 each, 18; p+q = 3: (3,0), (2,1), (1,2) → 4 each, 12; p+q = 4: (4,0), (3,1), (2,2), (1,3) → 1 each, 4. A circle of integer radius m centered at the origin passes through the 4 axis points, and through additional lattice points exactly when m has a prime factor ≡ 1 (mod 4); for m ≤ 12 that means m = 5 (3² + 4² = 25) and m = 10 (6² + 8² = 100), each giving 4 + 8 = 12 points. Its distance from the origin is |25|/√(9 + 16) = 5. The chord of the circle of radius 13 at distance 5 from its center has length 2√(169 − 25) = 2 · 12 = 24. "solution": "Disk A: x² + y² ≤ 25. Column counts for x = 0, ±1, ±2, ±3, ±4, ±5 are 11, 9, 9, 9, 7, 1, so |A| = 11 + 2(9+9+9+7+1) = 81. Disk B: (x−4)² + (y−3)² ≤ 9, a radius-3 disk around a lattice point; column counts for x − 4 = 0, ±1, ±2, ±3 are 7, 5, 5, 1, so |B| = 7 + 2(5+5+1) = 29.
